html.body: Date: 2025-03-17 REMARKSClaims 1-20 are pending, with claims 1, 11, and 19 being independent.Claims 11-18 have been withdrawn. Claims 1, 3, 10 and 19 have been amended.Claim 20 has been added. The amendment, addition, and/or withdrawal of claims is not to be considered in any way an indication of applicant's position on the merits of the original (pre-amendment) claims. In the following sections of the Amendment, the objections and rejections set forth in the December 16, 2024 Office Action are addressed. These rejections are respectfully traversed, and detailed arguments are set forth below.As a first preliminary matter, should this response not put this application in condition for allowance, to further prosecution, applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner contact the undersigned with suggestions that would put the claims into condition for allowance and, if the suggestions are acceptable, provide an Examiner's amendment to put the application into condition for allowance.As a second preliminary matter, the specification has been amended to correct grammatical and idiomatic errors of which applicant is aware. No new matter has been added in these amendments. It is submitted that these amendments should not be objectionable.Applicant has reviewed the Office Action and specifically disagrees with many of the assertions therein. For the purpose of furthering prosecution, however, applicant has chosen to focus on only the arguments set forth herein. Further, applicant has amended several claims for the purpose of furthering prosecution, but reserves the right to file continuation applications directed to the original claims. Applicant reserves the right to present additional arguments in future prosecution correspondence and/or in connection with continuation applications.Election/Restrictions Applicant has reviewed the Examiner's response and, while respectfully disagreeing, appreciates the detailed response.Applicant also appreciates the Examiner's acknowledgement that claim 19 is generic. Applicant also appreciates the Examiner's acknowledgment that if one or more generic claims are allowed, applicant is entitled to consideration of claims to additional species that depend from or otherwise require all of the limitations of an allowable generic claim as provided by 37 CFR 1.141.Drawings The September 20, 2024 Election Requirement identified Species A as being shown in FIGS. 2-10 and Species B as being shown in FIGS. 13-17. Applicant elected Species A. Page 5, lines 14-16 of the original specification states: "Preferred improved landing gear systems may include only a leverage-reducing landing gear system, only a constant angle suspension landing gear system, or both a leverage- reducing landing gear system and a constant angle suspension landing gear system." (There is similar language in the Abstract.) Similar language ("the leverage-reducing system 100 can be used in combination with the constant angle suspension mechanism 200") can be found at page 21, lines 28-29. Applicant would be willing to amend FIG.18 to show a plane that includes representations of Species A and Species B as follows:F G 18 Suggested FIG. 18 (above) shows that shown portion of Species A (e.g., the tires 102) is part of the leverage-reducing system 100 and the shown portion of Species B (e.g., the tires 202) is part of the constant angle suspension mechanism 200. As Species A is shown in the suggested FIG. 1 8. applicant respectfully submits that the election should include FIG. 18. along with FIGS. 2-10, as showing Species A. Although it would probably make the drawings unclear, applicant would be willing to amend one of FIGS.2-1 0 to include this subject matter.Regarding claim 10, if requested by the Examiner, applicant would be willing to add the specific reference numbers of the claimed "steerable tail wheel," "at least one third shock absorber," and "at least one constant angle suspension mechanism." The suggested FIG. 18 (above) only specifies the constant angle suspension mechanism 200, but points to other drawings showing examples of a constant angle suspension mechanism 200. Applicant respectfully submits that FIG. 18 would be the best place for those numbers if they were necessary.Regarding claim 19, if requested by the Examiner, applicant would be willing to add the specific reference numbers to the suggested FIG. 18 (above).Applicant respectfully submits that FIG. 18 would be the best place for those numbers if they were necessary.35 U.S.C. §112 As mentioned above, page 5, lines 14-16 of the original specification states: "Preferred improved landing gear systems may include only a leverage-reducing landing gear system, only a constant angle suspension landing gear system, or both a leverage-reducing landing gear system and a constant angle suspension landing gear system." (There is similar language in the Abstract.) Similar language ("the leverage- reducing system 100 can be used in combination with the constant angle suspension mechanism 200") can be found at page 21, lines 28-29. Applicant respectfully submits that the fact that these two systems could work together is clearly stated and claimed (see original claims 10 and 18).Although applicant specifically disagrees with the Examiner's characterization of the claims as indefinite, for the purpose of furthering prosecution, applicant has amended claims 1, 11, and 19 to positively recite the aircraft. Applicant respectfully submits that, as amended, these claims (and the claims dependent thereon) should no longer be indefinite. Applicant reserves the right to present additional arguments and/or pursue the original claims (or similar claims in which the aircraft is not positively claimed) in future prosecution communications and/or in connection with continuation applications.Applicant respectfully submits that the claim amendments overcome the 35 U.S.C. §112 rejections.35 U.S.C. §103 As a first preliminary matter, the Examiner incorrectly notes that the application named joint inventors. Please note that there is only a single inventor for this application.As a second preliminary matter, applicant is specifically not admitting that the structure of the cited references is equivalent to the claimed structure. For purposes of responding to this Office Action only (and specifically not as an admission), applicant had addressed structure of the references for the purpose it was cited by the Examiner.The fact that applicant is or is not responding to the rejection and characterizing the structure using the same terminology is not to be considered an admission that applicant agrees that the structure of the reference actually discloses the claimed structure.Claims 1-9 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0369381 to Jackson (the "Jackson reference").Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.In the paragraph beginning at page 3, line 9 of the original application, applicant described types of landing gear:Landing gear can be classified as fixed or retractable. Fixed landing gear (also referred to as "externally-mounted landing gear") is attached to the airframe and remains exposed to the slipstream as the aircraft is flown. As the speed of an aircraft increases, so does aerodynamic drag. Retractable landing gear retracts into the body of the aircraft and, thereby, reduces or eliminates aerodynamic drag. Aerodynamic drag is generally undesirable, but it becomes more problematic as speeds increase.The Jackson landing gear is retractable landing gear. It is described has having a stowed state 102 and a deployed state 104. Claim 19 (as amended) and new claim 20 specify that the landing gear is fixed landing gear.All of the pending claims specifically include "shock absorbers." The Examiner equates the claimed shock absorbers (examples of which are described at page 3, lines 21-22 as springs or self-contained hydraulic units that convert the impact forces into heat energy) with the Jackson actuators 250. The Jackson actuators are described in great detail in paragraphs 0041 to 0043. The purpose of the Jackson actuators is to selectively transition the landing gear assembly between a stowed state 102 and a deployed state 104. Jackson describes the actuator 250 as being "configured to selectively vary a distance between actuator link mount 252 and actuator aircraft mount 254 to transition the landing gear between stowed state 102 and deployed state 104." While examples of the actuator 250 are listed ("a hydraulic linear actuator, a hydraulic cylinder, a mechanical linear actuator, a pneumatic linear actuator, a pneumatic cylinder, and/or an electric linear actuator"), there is no indication that any of these exemplary actuators are shock absorbers equivalent to the claimed shock absorbers. Nor is there any indication that any of these exemplary actuators could perform a shock absorbing function. (The Jackson reference mentions that there may be shock absorbers in the elongate landing gear struts that could be configured to absorb the landing forces. (Paragraph 0047.)) If this rejection is maintained, applicant respectfully requests clarification.CONCLUDING REMARKSReconsideration of the claims is respectfully requested in view of the above amendments and remarks, and early notice of allowance thereof is earnestly solicited.If applicable, this should be considered a request under the provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) (Petition for Extension of Time) to extend the period for filing a reply in the above-identified application (for one, two, or three months, as necessary). The Director is hereby authorized to charge any fees which may be required, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account Number 60-4220. However, since the due date fell on a Saturday, applicant believes that no such extension fee is necessary.I hereby certify that this correspondence is being transmitted to the USPTO via Patent Center on the date (Eastern Standard Time) shown herein under the Rules of 37 CFR § 1.8.For the entire pendency of this application, or until authorization is revoked (e.g., using a specific revocation and/or changes to the Power of Attorney), the Director is authorized to charge Deposit Account No. 60-4220 for fee(s) necessary to effectuate the purpose of this filing. Please credit any overpayment of fees to the same Deposit Account.Respectfully submitted, Law Office of Karen Dana Oster, LLC /Karen Dana Oster/ Karen Dana Oster Reg.
